correctness.rationale: For distinct f,g choose coordinate i with f(i)!=g(i), and s_f(j)={f(j)} ∈M by Pairing for all j. Then f∈*s_f but g∉*s_f, so compatibility in first relation argument rules out f~g. Every congruence is equality. For at least two indices take constant-empty f and g with one singleton coordinate and another empty coordinate; they are distinct and have no ∈*-predecessors, so extensionality fails. Only equality is a relation congruence, so no quotient with membership well-defined can identify this witness. This is a symbolic all-I proof, no finite experiments or external Choice.
